_comment: Transport security on the GCP side, where the finding that matters is quieter than a
api-https is the one this check exists for. It is an HTTPS proxy with no SSL policy
attached, which is not a proxy without a policy — it is one running Google's default,
and that default negotiates down to TLS 1.0. No field on the resource says so. An estate
can be entirely HTTPS, hold no plaintext proxy at all, and still accept TLS 1.0 on every
path, which is the configuration a reviewer expects a compliance tool to catch.
internal-https names the failure explicitly instead: legacy-compatible is a real SSL
policy with minTlsVersion TLS_1_0. ghost-https names a policy the project did not list,
so the floor could not be resolved and it warns rather than being assumed acceptable.
web-redirect warns rather than failing — its URL map does nothing but redirect to HTTPS,
and failing the standard bare-hostname handler would put a permanent finding on a correct
configuration. legacy-http actually serves a map and fails.
For KSI-SVC-VCM, mesh-ledger is the interesting near-miss: it carries security settings,
so it is configured for a mesh, and has no clientTlsPolicy, so it is not validating the
peers in it. retired-service is declared and absent.
